passages.heading: New Course Proposal Walkthrough
passages.text:
New Course Proposal Walkthrough
New Course Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a New Course Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Navigate by Section
Related toolkit entry: Specialization Modification Proposal Walkthrough

passages.heading: Understand URI’s Curricular Process
passages.text:
Familiarize yourself with URI’s curricular process before beginning your proposal. This will help you understand the steps involved in the curricular process and accurately estimate how long your proposal may take to reach approval.
How the Curriculum Process Works
Related toolkit entry: How the Curriculum Process Works
Approval Calendar
Related toolkit entry: Approval Calendar

passages.heading: Make Sure You Can Access Kuali CM
passages.text:
You will need access to Kuali Curriculum Management (Kuali CM) to propose any curricular item.
Kuali Basics
Related toolkit entry: Kuali Basics

passages.heading: Choose the Right Proposal Type
passages.text:
Some course proposal types can be easily confused. If you are unsure which type applies, review these common examples.
Table columns: If you want to… | Use…
If you want to…: Make a Temporary Course a Permanent Course which appears in the Academic Catalog | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Create a new cross-listing to accompany an existing course | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Add a new topic to an open-ended topics course | Use…: New Course Proposal if the course is a GCH course No proposal needed for any other subject code. Contact Enrollment Services to add the new topic.
If you want to…: Add a new topic to a permanent topics course | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Create a new 500-level section of a course to accompany the 400-level | Use…: New Course Proposal

passages.heading: Start the Proposal
passages.text:
From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Courses.
On the Courses page, select + New Course in the upper-right corner.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

passages.heading: Contact Information
passages.text:
Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.

passages.heading: Course Administration
passages.text:
Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the course to become effective. If the effective term entered at proposal submission has missed the deadline by the time it reaches the Faculty Senate, this field will be automatically updated to the next available semester.
Academic Career Select the appropriate Academic Career from the available options. You may only choose one option. If you plan to offer this course in both the traditional and accelerated calendars, please provide a rationale in the Supporting Materials file upload gadget that comes after the description.
College Select the college in which the course is housed.
Department Select the department in which the course is housed.
Honors Program Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Honors Program.
Honors Type Select HPR Course or H-section of Existing Course.
General Education Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “No” is chosen for General Education.
Temporary Course Select Yes or No.

passages.heading: Course Information
passages.text:
Subject Code The subject code must be owned by the College and Department previously entered in the form.
Number A validation error will occur if you use a number already in use by the subject code. The course numbering system is found in UM 8.30.10.
Temporary course numbers end with an “X”
Grand Challenge course numbers end with a “G”
Is this a 400-level course available for graduate credit? Required for all courses. Select Yes or No, regardless of the course level.
Course Title
Abbreviated Course Title 29-characters max.
Course Description Course descriptions are written for students, not faculty, and must communicate clearly and concisely to them. Jargon, acronyms, and technical language should be avoided as much as possible. Anyone should be able to read the description and understand the nature and intent of the course.
URI course descriptions include additional course information such as credits, cross-listed courses, method of instruction, class hours, requisites, grading, graduate credit, and general education outcomes. Descriptions will be formatted to the catalog standard prior to final approval.

passages.heading: Course Information
passages.text: Supporting Materials Optional. Use this file upload to provide additional information that may be helpful to review committees before the proposal enters the approval workflow.

passages.heading: Modality, Method of Instruction, and Prerequisites
passages.text:
Modality Select all applicable options to indicate whether the course will be offered in person, online, or both. The specific modalities are provided for reference next to the checkboxes and are also defined in University Manual 8.30.30
Method of Instruction All courses must have at least one method of instruction. Note that “Online” is not a method of instruction; it was removed from the list of methods of instruction in 2025.
If the course has multiple methods of instruction, select the first as Primary and all additional methods as Secondary.
If the course has two or more methods of instruction, indicate how the methods are divided. This information is important for Enrollment Services; omitting it may delay final approval.
Requisites Can include prerequisites, corequisites, antirequisites, or other enrollment requirements.

passages.heading: Cross-listed Courses
passages.text:
Is this a cross-listed course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this a cross-listed course?
Cross-listed course(s) for eCampus Click “Add New” to add all cross-listings.
Cross-listed course(s) for the Catalog Click the “+” and add all cross-listings again.
Cross-listed Department(s) Add all departments belonging to the cross-listed courses, even if one or more belong to the same department.
Letter(s) of support from cross-listed departments For new courses and course modifications, the “parent” department (the department associated with the course code on the proposal) must provide a letter of support from each cross-listed department.
What if my cross-listed course code belongs to the same department as the parent course code? For example, MCE and ISE are both in the Department of Mechanical, Industrial & Systems Engineering.
Just upload a document stating: “Both subject codes belong to the same department.”

passages.heading: Grading Method, Credits, and Repeat Criteria
passages.text:
Credits First, select whether the course has fixed credits or a credit range. Then enter the applicable credit amount(s) in the fields provided.
Grading Method Select letter grades, S/U, or both.
Can this course be repeated for credit? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can this course be repeated for credit?
Maximum times course may be taken: Enter max number of times.
Maximum credits allowed: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn for the course. For example, a 3-credit course that may be taken three times for credit has a maximum of 9 credits.
Can students repeat within the same term? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can students repeat within the same term?
Maximum credits allowed per term: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn from this course within a single term.

passages.heading: New Course Considerations
passages.text:
Explain the purpose of the course. Enter a brief explanation of the course's purpose.
How is this course used within the curriculum? Select the appropriate option from the provided radio buttons.
🔽 The following field will appear only if if Core requirement… is chosen from How is this course used within the curriculum?
List all degree, major, minor, and certificate programs for which this course is required. List the name of all applicable programs for which the course is a required component.
By checking this box, I acknowledge that all courses must be approved via Faculty Senate vote before a program can be reviewed for final approval. Check the box to acknowledge that the course must receive Faculty Senate approval before a program requiring the course can receive final approval.
Content Overlap: Has the proposed course been discussed with any academic units that may have related or overlapping curricular interests? Select Yes or Not Applicable.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is chosen from Has the proposed course been discussed with any academic units…?

passages.heading: New Course Considerations
passages.text: Supporting Documentation Provide documentation demonstrating consultation with departments that have related or potentially overlapping curricular interests.

passages.heading: Certification for New Courses by Originating Academic Unit
passages.text:
This section is completed by the Department Chair or, when applicable, the Director, Area Coordinator, or College Curriculum Committee Chair. Proposers should leave this section blank and proceed to the next section.
For those responsible for completing this section:
Certification by the Department Chair, Director, or Area Coordinator responsible for administering the course. Check the box to certify that the proposal has received the required approval by the faculty of the originating academic unit.
Name of Department Chairperson, Director, or Area Coordinator Enter your name.
Date of Faculty Vote Enter the date the faculty voted on the proposal.

passages.heading: General Education Outcomes
passages.text:
🔽 This section will appear only if Yes is chosen from General Education.
Learning Outcome 1 Select the appropriate learning outcome from the dropdown and complete the table for your first outcome.
Learning Outcome 2 Courses must have at least one General Education learning outcome and may have up to two. Based on your selection for Learning Outcome 1, the applicable options will be available in this dropdown. If you are not adding a second outcome, leave this field blank.
If selected, complete the table for your second outcome.
Is this a grand challenge? Select Yes or No.

passages.heading: Grand Challenge
passages.text:
🔽 This section will appear only if the course is for general education credit, and if Yes is chosen for Is this a grand challenge?
To qualify for the grand challenge overlay, complete the following questions.
GRAND CHALLENGE: Explain how the course title, syllabus, and assignments demonstrate the contemporary challenge addressed by the course.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Explain how the course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and provides opportunities for students to make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Provide an abbreviated reading list organized by discipline that demonstrates the course’s disciplinary perspectives, and explain how each disciplinary perspective is integrated into major course assignments and activities.
ETHICS: Identify the ethical framework that allows students to weigh/evaluate issues. This topic needs to show up explicitly in the course schedule.
ETHICS: List the readings pertaining to ethics.
ETHICS: Describe how ethics is incorporated in some/all of the assignments and activities.

passages.heading: Library Impact Statement
passages.text:
Once the proposal is submitted to the workflow, it is automatically routed to the Library Subject Selector, who will complete and upload the Library Impact Statement. Other than completing the prompts in this section, no additional action is required from the proposer.
Supplementary resources you expect to use in proposed course Select all that apply.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Other is chosen from Supplementary resources...
If Other, please specify:
Will students conduct library research in this course? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if YES is chosen from Will students conduct library research...?
Please describe assignment(s) in detail.
LIST the critical journals, monographs, and electronic resources in the field that the University Library MUST have in order to support this course or program:
LIST any additional journals, monographs and electronic resources in the field that would support the course, but are NOT essential:
Library Impact Statement Document The Library Subject Selector will upload this to the proposal after the proposer submits to the workflow.

passages.heading: Submit to the Workflow
passages.text:
Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.
Select Submit for Approval to submit the proposal to the workflow.

passages.heading: So, what happens now?
passages.text: Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.

Course Modification Proposal Walkthrough
This guide provides step-by-step procedural instructions for completing and submitting a Course Modification Proposal in Kuali. It focuses on navigating the form, including what to select or enter in each field.
The guide is organized by proposal section (panel), so you can jump directly to a section when you need help.
This guide does not provide guidance on course content or academic decisions. Consult your department and applicable curriculum committees for questions about developing the course itself.
Related toolkit entry: Specialization Modification Proposal Walkthrough

passages.heading: Understand URI’s Curricular Process
passages.text:
Familiarize yourself with URI’s curricular process before beginning your proposal. This will help you understand the steps involved in the curricular process and accurately estimate how long your proposal may take to reach approval.
How the Curriculum Process Works

Related toolkit entry: Approval Calendar

passages.heading: Make Sure You Can Access Kuali CM
passages.text:
You will need access to Kuali Curriculum Management (Kuali CM) to propose any curricular item.
Kuali Basics
Related toolkit entry: Kuali Basics

passages.heading: Choose the Right Proposal Type
passages.text:
Some course proposal types can be easily confused. If you are unsure which type applies, review these common examples.
Table columns: If you want to… | Use…
If you want to…: Make a Temporary Course a Permanent Course which appears in the Academic Catalog | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Create a new cross-listing to accompany an existing course | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Add a new topic to an open-ended topics course | Use…: New Course Proposal if the course is a GCH course No proposal needed for any other subject code. Contact Enrollment Services to add the new topic.
If you want to…: Add a new topic to a permanent topics course | Use…: Course Modification Proposal
If you want to…: Create a new 500-level section of a course to accompany the 400-level | Use…: New Course Proposal

passages.heading: Start the Proposal
passages.text:
From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Courses.
On the Courses page, use the search bar at the top to find the course you would like to modify. You can search by:
Course code (e.g., COM100)
Course title (e.g., Communication Fundamentals)
Keywords found in the course title, description, or anywhere in the course form.
Once you locate the course, select it to open the current version
With the current course open, select Propose Changes in the upper-right corner of the window.
A window will appear prompting you to select Create a new version or Create a new revision. Always select Create a new version.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

passages.heading: Course Modification Proposal
passages.text:
This is where you will indicate the changes you are proposing to make to the course.
Select the type(s) of change: Check Major, Minor, or both, depending on the changes you are proposing. If you’re not sure which category applies, that’s okay! Select an option to view the list of changes included in that category.
Select the specific change(s): From the list(s) that appear, check the box next to each Major and/or Minor change you are proposing.

passages.heading: Change the course description
passages.text:
Modify the description of a course. For example: Introduces students to the principles of environmental sustainability, with emphasis on climate change, resource management, and sustainable practices and their applications in modern society.
See Course Description
Related toolkit entry: Course Description

passages.heading: Add or change a modality
passages.text:
Add: Add a new modality to a course (e.g., add an in-person option to an online course). Change: Change the modality in which a course is offered (e.g., change an in-person course to online).
See Modality
Related toolkit entry: Modality

passages.heading: Change the method of instruction
passages.text:
Change the method of instruction for a course (e.g., Lecture to Seminar or Lecture to Lecture and Recitation).
See Method of Instruction
Related toolkit entry: Method of Instruction

passages.heading: Change the course number to a new hundred level
passages.text:
Change a course number to a different hundred level (e.g., BIO318 to BIO418).
See Course Number
Related toolkit entry: Course Number

passages.heading: Add new general education outcomes
passages.text:
Add GE outcomes to a course that does not currently have any, or add a new GE outcome to a course that already has been approved for GE (this may involve replacing an existing outcome, or adding a second outcome to a course currently approved for only one).
See General Education Outcomes
Related toolkit entry: General Education Outcomes

passages.heading: Add new topic to GCH course
passages.text:
Because GCH courses carry General Education outcomes, each new topic must be reviewed by the General Education Committee.
See GCH Topics
Related toolkit entry: GCH Topics

passages.heading: Change the grading method of a GE course
passages.text:
All GE outcomes must have a grading method of Letter Grades, with the exception of D1 which can also be graded as S/U. Therefore, this only applies to D1 courses.
See Grading Method
Related toolkit entry: Grading Method

passages.heading: Change number of fixed credits
passages.text:
Change the number of fixed credits for a course (e.g., 3 to 4 credits).
See Credits.
Related toolkit entry: Credits

passages.heading: Change fixed credits to a credit range
passages.text:
Change a course with fixed credits (e.g., 3 credits) to a credit range (e.g., 3–4 credits or 1–3 credits).
See Credits

passages.heading: Change the credit range outside of current range
passages.text:
Change a course’s credit range from 3–6 credits to a range that falls outside of 3–6 credits (e.g., 1–6, 3–12, or 1–12).
See Credits

passages.heading: Change varied credits to a fixed credit outside of current range
passages.text:
Change a course with a credit range (e.g., 3–6 credits) to a fixed number of credits outside the current range (e.g., 2 credits or 7 credits).
See Credits

passages.heading: Add graduate credit to a 400-level course
passages.text: Allow a 400-level course to count for graduate credit, either as an elective in a graduate program or for double counting in an ABM program.

passages.heading: Delete course
passages.text: Remove the course from the University’s course offerings, the catalog, and inactivate it in eCampus.

passages.heading: Change course title
passages.text:
Introduction to Digital Media and Design Fundamentals
SeeCourse Title
Related toolkit entry: Course Title

passages.heading: Change academic home (department / college)
passages.text: Move a course from one department or college to another.

passages.heading: Remove a modality
passages.text:
Remove one of the modalities in which a course is currently offered, so that the course is offered in only one modality (in-person / online)
See Modality

passages.heading: Change prerequisites
passages.text: Add, remove, or change a course prerequisite.

passages.heading: Change subject code
passages.text: Change the subject code assigned to a course, such as changing BIO to CMB.

passages.heading: Add a cross-listing
passages.text:
Add a new cross-listed subject code to a course. For example: MBA545 becomes MBA545(BUS545), or MBA543(BUS543) adds FIN543, becoming MBA543 (BUS543, FIN543).
SeeCross-listed Course
Related toolkit entry: Cross-listed Course

passages.heading: Remove a cross-listing
passages.text:
Remove an existing cross-listed subject code from a course. For example: MBA543(BUS543, FIN543) becomes MBA543(BUS543).
SeeCross-listed Course

passages.heading: Remove general education outcomes
passages.text: Remove one or more general education outcomes from a course.

passages.heading: Change temporary course to permanent
passages.text:
Make a temporary course permanent so that it can continue to be offered beyond the two times permitted within the two years after approval.
See Temporary Course
Related toolkit entry: Temporary Course

passages.heading: Change open ended topic course type (permanent topics vs. temporary topics)
passages.text:
Change whether an open-ended course is offered with permanent topics or temporary topics. Permanent topics are listed in the course description, while temporary topics are not.
See Topics Course
Related toolkit entry: Topics Course

passages.heading: Change grading method of a non-GE course
passages.text:
Change whether a non-General Education course is graded using letter grades, S/U grading, or both.
See Grading Method

passages.heading: Change course number within the hundred level
passages.text: Change a course number while keeping it within the same hundred level (e.g., BIO101 to BIO105).

passages.heading: Change credit range inside of the current range
passages.text:
Narrow a course’s credit range without changing its existing minimum or maximum credits (e.g., 1–6 credits to 2–5 credits).
See Credits

passages.heading: Change varied credits to fixed credits within current range
passages.text:
Change a course with a credit range to a fixed number of credits that falls within the current range (e.g., 3–6 credits to 4 credits).
See Credits

passages.heading: Change course repeat criteria
passages.text:
Change the conditions under which a course may be repeated for credit.
See Repeat Criteria
Related toolkit entry: Repeat Criteria

passages.heading: Remove graduate credit from a 400-level course
passages.text:
Remove the option for a 400-level course to count for graduate credit.
Rationale Briefly describe the rationale for the proposed changes.
🔽 The following field will appear only if a syllabus is required based on the checkboxes selected above.
Syllabus Upload the course syllabus here.

passages.heading: Contact Information
passages.text:
Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.

passages.heading: Course Administration
passages.text:
Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the course to become effective. If the effective term entered at proposal submission has missed the deadline by the time it reaches the Faculty Senate, this field will be automatically updated to the next available semester.
Academic Career This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless one of the following applies:
The course number or level is changing. For example, an undergraduate-level course is becoming a graduate-level course, or vice versa.
The course is moving from the Traditional Calendar to the Accelerated Online Calendar, or vice versa.
Changing the Academic Calendar?
Good to know: If a course is already approved for online instruction, you do not need a proposal to offer it in the other academic calendar, as long as it will remain online. You can simply contact Enrollment Services to schedule the course in the other calendar.
A proposal is required when the change also involves a change in modality (for example, changing from online to in-person).
Which situation applies to you?

passages.heading: Adding an Accelerated Online (7-week) section of a course already approved for online instruction?
passages.text: No proposal is needed as long as there are no other changes to the course. Contact Enrollment Services to schedule the course in the Accelerated Online Calendar.

passages.heading: Adding a Traditional (14-week) online section of a course already approved for online instruction in the Accelerated Online Calendar?
passages.text: No proposal is needed as long as there are no other changes to the course. Contact Enrollment Services to schedule the course in the Traditional Calendar.

passages.heading: Adding an Accelerated Online (7-week) section of a course currently approved only for in-person instruction?
passages.text:
A proposal is required because you are adding a new modality. On the proposal, keep the original 14-week calendar radio button selected under Academic Calendar. In your rationale, explain that you intend to continue offering the course in the Traditional Calendar while also adding an online section to the Accelerated Online Calendar.
Example: “We want to continue to offer this course in the Traditional Calendar, as well as add an online section to the Accelerated Online Calendar.”

passages.heading: Adding an in-person section to a course currently approved only for the Accelerated Online (7-week) Calendar?
passages.text:
A proposal is required because you are adding a new modality. On the proposal, keep the original 7-week accelerated calendar radio button selected under Academic Calendar. In your rationale, explain that you intend to continue offering the course in the Accelerated Online Calendar while also adding an in-person section to the Traditional Calendar.
Example: “We want to continue to offer this course in the Accelerated Online Calendar, as well as add an in-person section to the Traditional Calendar.”
College This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change academic home (department/college) in the first section of the form.
Department This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change academic home (department/college) in the first section of the form.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Change academic home was checked.
Letter(s) of support from outgoing department / college. Upload confirmation from the original department/college that they are in support of the course moving to a new academic home.
Honors Program This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.

passages.heading: Adding an in-person section to a course currently approved only for the Accelerated Online (7-week) Calendar?
passages.text:
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Honors Program.
Honors Type This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
General Education This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Add new general education outcomes (and the course was not GE previously), or Remove general education outcomes in the first section of the form.

passages.heading: Course Information
passages.text:
Subject Code This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change subject code in the first section of the form.
Remember: The subject code must be owned by the College and Department previously entered in the form.
Number This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change course number within the hundred level or Change course number to a new hundred level in the first section of the form. A few reminders:
The course numbering system is found in UM 8.30.10.
Temporary course numbers end with an “X”
Grand Challenge course numbers end with a “G”
Is this a 400-level course available for graduate credit? This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Add graduate credit to a 400-level course or Remove graduate from a 400-level course in the first section of the form.
Course Title This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change course title in the first section of the form.

passages.heading: Course Information
passages.text:
Abbreviated Course Title This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change course title in the first section of the form.
Course Description This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you are changing the course description, the general education outcomes, the grading method, the repeat criteria, the credits or credit range, removing or adding 400-level for graduate credit, the prerequisites, the cross-listing(s), or the repeat criteria. (Click on the Course Description link for more information).
Supporting Materials Optional. Use this file upload to provide additional information that may be helpful to review committees before the proposal enters the approval workflow.

passages.heading: Modality, Method of Instruction, and Prerequisites
passages.text:
Modality This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Add or change a modality in the first section of the form.
Method of Instruction This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Change the method of instruction in the first section of the form.
Note that “Online” is not a method of instruction; it was removed from the list of methods of instruction in 2025. If this still remains entered in your proposal, please change it.
If the course has multiple methods of instruction, select the first as Primary and all additional methods as Secondary.
If the course has two or more methods of instruction, indicate how the methods are divided. This information is important for Enrollment Services; omitting it may delay final approval.
Requisites Confirm the prerequisites in this textbox. Copy them exactly as they are listed in the description unless you have checked Change prerequisites in the first section of the form.

passages.heading: Cross-listed Courses
passages.text:
Is this a cross-listed course? This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked Add a cross-listing or Remove a cross-listing in the first section of the form.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Is this a cross-listed course?
Cross-listed course(s) for eCampus Make sure all cross-listed courses are entered (existing and proposed)
Cross-listed course(s) for the Catalog Make sure all cross-listed courses are entered here as well (existing and proposed).
Cross-listed Department(s) Make sure all departments are entered here which belong to the cross-listed courses (existing and proposed).
Letter(s) of support from cross-listed departments For new courses and course modifications, the “parent” department (the department associated with the course code on the proposal) must provide a letter of support from each cross-listed department.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Remove a cross-listing is checked in the first section of the form.
Letter(s) of support from removed cross-listed department(s) Upload confirmation and support from the department of the proposed removed cross-listed course.

passages.heading: Cross-listed Courses
passages.text:
What if my cross-listed course code belongs to the same department as the parent course code? For example, MCE and ISE are both in the Department of Mechanical, Industrial & Systems Engineering.
Just upload a document stating: “Both subject codes belong to the same department.”

passages.heading: Grading Method, Credits, and Repeat Criteria
passages.text:
Credits This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you have checked one of the following in the first section of the form:
Change number of fixed credits
Change fixed credits to a credit range
Change the credit range outside of current range
Change varied credits to a fixed credit outside of current range
Change credit range inside of the current range
Change varied credits to fixed credits within current range
Grading Method Select letter grades, S/U, or both.
Can this course be repeated for credit? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can this course be repeated for credit?
Maximum times course may be taken: Enter max number of times.
Maximum credits allowed: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn for the course. For example, a 3-credit course that may be taken three times for credit has a maximum of 9 credits.
Can students repeat within the same term? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if “Yes” is chosen for Can students repeat within the same term?
Maximum credits allowed per term: Enter the maximum number of credits a student may earn from this course within a single term.

passages.heading: General Education Outcomes
passages.text:
🔽 This section will appear only if Yes is chosen from General Education.
If this course is already approved for general education, the following fields will already be populated.
Proposers do not need to fill out the outcome tables for outcomes already approved. However, tables for new outcomes need to be filled out according to the requirements.
Learning Outcome 1 Select the appropriate learning outcome from the dropdown and complete the table for your first outcome.
Learning Outcome 2 Courses must have at least one General Education learning outcome and may have up to two. Based on your selection for Learning Outcome 1, the applicable options will be available in this dropdown. If you are not adding a second outcome, leave this field blank.
If selected, complete the table for your second outcome.
Is this a grand challenge? Select Yes or No.

passages.heading: Grand Challenge
passages.text:
🔽 This section will appear only if the course is for general education credit, and if Yes is chosen for Is this a grand challenge?
If this course is already approved for the Grand Challenge, you do not need to complete the following fields. Because Grand Challenge courses were established before Kuali, some fields may not have existing information. If you are required to enter something in a text field in order to submit the proposal to workflow, you may enter “—”.
GRAND CHALLENGE: Explain how the course title, syllabus, and assignments demonstrate the contemporary challenge addressed by the course.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Explain how the course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and provides opportunities for students to make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences.
INTERDISCIPLINARY: Provide an abbreviated reading list organized by discipline that demonstrates the course’s disciplinary perspectives, and explain how each disciplinary perspective is integrated into major course assignments and activities.

passages.heading: Grand Challenge
passages.text:
ETHICS: Identify the ethical framework that allows students to weigh/evaluate issues. This topic needs to show up explicitly in the course schedule.
ETHICS: List the readings pertaining to ethics.
ETHICS: Describe how ethics is incorporated in some/all of the assignments and activities.

passages.heading: Submit to the Workflow
passages.text:
Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.
Select Submit for Approval to submit the proposal to the workflow.

passages.heading: So, what happens now?
passages.text: Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.

passages.heading: Choose the Right Proposal Type
passages.text:
If you are unsure which type applies to your proposal, review the examples below.
Table columns: If you want to… | Use…
If you want to…: Change the requirements of a major or degree program | Use…: Program modification proposal
If you want to…: Change the requirements to a major or degree program, and it’s specializations (options, tracks, sub-plans). | Use…: Program modification proposal and specialization modification proposal (one for each existing specialization that you want to change)
If you want to…: Change only the requirements of one specialization of a major or degree program | Use…: Specialization modification proposal
If you want to…: Create an Accelerated Online Version of an existing program | Use…: New program proposal
If you want to…: Change the title of a program while teaching-out the original name. | Use…: New program proposal - to create new title Program modification proposal - to suspend admission to old title
If you want to…: Create a new program with specializations | Use…: New program proposal and new specialization(s) proposal(s)
If you want to…: Create a 4+1 Pathway | Use…: New specialization proposal, inherited to the Bachelors degree.

passages.heading: Choose the Right Proposal Type
passages.text: If you want to…: Create an ABM program | Use…: New specialization proposal, inherited to the Masters degree.

passages.heading: Start the Proposal
passages.text:
From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).
Select Curriculum to open your Dashboard .
Related toolkit entry: Dashboard
From the left-hand navigation menu, select Programs.
On the Programs page, use the search bar at the top to find the course you would like to modify. You can search by:
Degree Title (e.g., Bachelor of Music, or Bachelor of Arts)
Major Title (e.g., Environmental Arts & Humanities)
Keywords found in the description, or anywhere in the course form.
Once you locate the program, select it to open the current version
With the current program open, select Propose Changes in the upper-right corner of the window.
A window will appear prompting you to select Create a new version or Create a new revision. Always select Create a new version.
The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.

passages.heading: Program Modification
passages.text: Select the applicable changes in the checkboxes/radio buttons.

passages.heading: Contact Information
passages.text:
Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program.
Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.

passages.heading: Program Information
passages.text:
Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the program to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term with Modifications Select the term and year in which you anticipate the students will graduate with the changes proposed.
Credential Type This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Level This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Academic Calendar This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Important Information about Changing a Program’s Academic Calendar
If a program is currently offered on the Traditional Academic Calendar and you would like to move it to the Accelerated Academic Calendar, you cannot simply change the calendar while students are still enrolled in the program. The existing program must first be fully taught out. This requires a proposal to suspend admission to the program. Once there are no students remaining in the program, the program can be moved from one academic calendar to the other.

passages.heading: Modality
passages.text:
Modality
Tags: courses,programs,specializations
Short Description: Identifies how a curricular offering is delivered, including in-person, online, or a combination of in-person and online instruction.
Modality
Modality identifies the method of delivery for a curricular offering, including courses, programs, and specializations. It describes whether instruction occurs in person, online, or through a combination of in-person and online instruction.
The University recognizes the following modalities:

passages.heading: In-Person Modalities
passages.text:
In Person
Instruction occurs at a specified physical location on specified days and times. Less than 25% of instruction is delivered online.
In Person & Online Asynchronous
Instruction combines in-person meetings on specified days and times with online asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and weekly time commitment for online asynchronous instruction must be clear to students in the syllabus on the first day of class. Neither modality may account for less than 25% of total instructional time.
In Person & Online Synchronous
Instruction combines in-person and online meetings on specified days and times. Neither modality may account for less than 25% of total instructional time.

passages.heading: Online Modalities
passages.text:
Online Synchronous
All instruction occurs online at specified days and times.
Online Synchronous & Asynchronous
All instruction occurs online and combines synchronous meetings on specified days and times with asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and weekly time commitment for online asynchronous instruction must be clear to students in the syllabus. Neither modality may account for less than 25% of total instructional time.
Online Asynchronous
All instruction occurs online with no required synchronous meetings at specified days and times, except for optional online office hours or meetings. The weekly time commitment for online asynchronous instruction must be clear to students in the syllabus.
See University Manual 8.30.30

passages.heading: The Outcomes

The General Education program will assess student exposure to twelve Student Learning Outcomes in four areas:
A. Build knowledge of diverse peoples and cultures and of the natural and physical world.
(A1) STEM Disciplines (A2) Social & Behavioral Sciences (A3) Humanities (A4) Art & Design
B. Develop intellectual and interdisciplinary competencies for academic and lifelong learning.
(B1) Write Effectively (B2) Communicate Effectively (B3) Mathematical, Statistical, or Computational Strategies (B4) Information Literacy
C. Exercise individual and social responsibilities.
(C1) Civic Knowledge & Responsibilies (C2) Global Responsibility (C3) Diversity & Inclusion
D. Integrate and apply these abilities and capacities, adapting them to new settings, questions, and responsibilities to lay the foundation for lifelong learning.
(D1) Integrate & Apply

passages.heading: Syllabus
passages.text:
Syllabus
Tags: courses
Short Description: A roadmap for a course that communicates its scope, learning outcomes, expectations, policies, assessments, and other essential information students need to successfully complete the course.
Syllabus
University Manual 8.50.30 Course Syllabi. All instructors shall make available a syllabus in the first week of class, or first day of class for fully-online accelerated programs (8.51.24), to students enrolled in each of their courses. Syllabi components should clearly communicate classroom policies, essential aspects of the course, and expectations of student participation.
University Manual 8.51.24 For online courses taught in the fully-online accelerated calendar, final projects and/or final exams shall be scheduled by faculty according to the learning outcomes of the class and best pedagogical practices for online learning. The calendar of due dates for assignments and assessments shall be in the syllabus and available to students on the first day of class. No final exam or final project shall be due after the last day of the session.
From the Provost:

passages.heading: Syllabus
passages.text: In addition to satisfying Faculty Senate approved policies, your syllabus communicates mutual expectations between you and your students and serves as a roadmap to successful course completion, including your course scope, expectations, learning outcomes, deadlines, attendance policies, grading criteria, and other important information. Please provide students with information about assessment/major paper/project due dates, office hours, availability of special tutorial sessions, and expectations on individual vs group work. This clear outlining of expectations helps to ensure that students in your classes understand what they are expected to learn, how they will be assessed, and are fully aware of your academic standards. Providing such information can help avoid misunderstanding, frustration—on both sides—and foster acceptance of responsibility by our students

passages.heading: Temporary Course
passages.text:
Temporary Course
Tags: courses
Short Description: A course approved for limited offerings, typically to test an experimental course or address a temporary need. Also known as an “X-Course.”
Temporary Course
UM 8.80.12 A temporary course may be offered no more than twice and only during a two-year period following its approval. A temporary course must meet one or more of the following criteria: a) it is experimental in nature. It is innovative, using unconventional devices or pedagogical methods, course materials, approach to course content or student-teacher relationships; b) it is being tried out on a temporary basis so that its value and effectiveness can be tested before it is added to a department’s permanent curriculum; c) it is intended for a limited duration, such as in the case of employing a visiting specialist temporarily available or to satisfy temporary needs and interests of students or to deal with timely issues.

passages.heading: Temporary Course
passages.text: UM 8.81.30 A Temporary Course shall have approval of the department(s) or committee proposing it, the dean(s) of the college(s) involved, and the Curriculum and Standards Committee and/or the Graduate Council, except that a temporary University College mini-course (a one-credit lower-level undergraduate course taught during the fall or spring semester) does not require the approval of the Curriculum and Standards Committee. The Curriculum and Standards Committee shall, however, receive information about any temporary University College mini-course after it has been approved by the college dean. The Graduate Council may refuse to grant or may attach conditions to the granting of graduate program credit for a temporary course. Each college may require internal channels of approval in addition to those specified here.

passages.heading: Temporary Course
passages.text:
UM 8.81.31 The Curriculum and Standards Committee and the Graduate Council shall give priority at their meetings to the consideration of proposed temporary courses. Prior to approving temporary courses, these committees shall distribute to all faculty a description of these courses and shall provide faculty members with a seven-day period in which to register comments with the Chairperson of the Curriculum and Standards Committee and/or with the Dean of the Graduate School.
UM 8.81.60 It is the responsibility of the Office of Enrollment Services to limit the offering of a temporary course to only twice during a two-year period and to limit to three times the offering of a specific topic within an open-ended course.

passages.heading: Course Number
passages.text:
Course Number
Tags: courses
Short Description: The numerical portion of a course identifier that follows the Subject Code (e.g., ENG101, where ENG is the Subject Code and 101 is the Course Number).
Course Number

passages.heading: 001-099 Level.
passages.text: Pre-freshman and special undergraduate. Characteristics: Undergraduate courses not applicable for degree credit. Post-Secondary or sub-freshman remedial courses, Alan Shawn Feinstein College of Education and Professional Studies courses for no credit or for non-credit certificate credit only.

passages.heading: 100-299 Level.
passages.text: Lower division undergraduate courses. Primarily for freshmen and sophomores and as electives for upper class students. Characteristics: Little or no prior college level work required. May not be taken for graduate credit.

passages.heading: 300-399 Level.
passages.text: Upper division undergraduate courses. Primarily for juniors and seniors majoring in the field or advanced students in other disciplines. Characteristics: Some formal background or sophistication required but not to the extent that would ordinarily justify allowing graduate degree credit.

passages.heading: 400-499* Level.
passages.text:
Generally limited to juniors and seniors majoring in the field. Open to other advanced undergraduates and to graduate students with permission. Characteristics: Extensive background required, may be taken for graduate credit. (Limitations may be stated by the department if desired.)
Courses numbered at the 400 level that are available for graduate credit must be approved by both the appropriate Undergraduate Curriculum Committee (CASC or GEC) and the Graduate Council.

passages.heading: 500-599 Level.
passages.text: Graduate level courses. The bachelor’s degree is usually a prerequisite but qualified seniors and honors students can be admitted with permission. Characteristics: Comprise majority of course work between bachelor’s and master’s degree. Number 599 reserved for masters thesis research and is graded on an S/U-only basis.

passages.heading: 600-699 Level.
passages.text: Advanced graduate courses. No undergraduates admitted except honors students with approval of advisors and the department. Characteristics: Comprise majority of course work between master’s and doctor’s degree but not limited to doctoral students. Number 699 reserved for doctoral thesis research and is graded on an S/U-only basis.

passages.heading: 900-999 Level.
passages.text:
Special types of graduate courses for which no program credit is allowed. Characteristics: Workshops, institutes, courses taken for certificate credit only, courses taken to remedy deficiencies, and temporary courses which have not been approved by the Graduate Council for graduate program credit.

passages.heading: Degree / Major Program Requirements
passages.text:
Undergraduate programs are required to have a minimum or 120 credits, and a maximum of 148 (UM 8.21.10)
Undergraduate programs shall include at least 6 credits of free electives (UM 8.21.10)
General Education requirements shall apply to all undergraduate programs (UM 8.21.11)
A cumulative average of at least 2.00 is required to graduate from all undergraduate degrees. (UM 8.22.10)
Master’s degree programs with thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. 18 must be from content-based courses, 6 must be thesis courses. (GSM 7.44.1)
Master’s degree programs without thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. (GSM 7.45.1)
Doctoral students must complete a Program of Study with a minimum of 64 credit hours beyond the undergraduate degree (GSM 7.54) (See GSM sections 7.54 and 7.21)
In Kuali, the term program refers to all credential types; Degrees, majors, minors, and certificates. In the Manual, program refers to a graduate student’s major field of study.

passages.heading: What is Kuali Curriculum Management?
passages.text: Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is URI’s system for managing university curriculum and the curriculum approval process. It uses electronic forms and workflow to route course, program, and specialization proposals through the appropriate levels of review and approval.

passages.heading: Kuali, the Catalog, and eCampus
passages.text:
Kuali serves as the central source for approved curriculum information:
Kuali CM — Manages curriculum proposals and the approval workflow.
Academic Catalog — Pulls approved course, program, and specialization information from Kuali.
eCampus — Receives approved course information from Kuali for implementation in future terms.

passages.heading: Why it matters
passages.text: Information entered into Kuali can flow directly into the official academic catalog and eCampus. Proposals should therefore be clear, accurate, and unambiguous, as the information entered during the proposal process becomes part of the University’s official curriculum.

passages.heading: Access & Logging Into Kuali
passages.text: Access to Kuali CM is limited to faculty, Deans, and select administrators and staff. Only faculty members may submit curriculum proposals.

passages.heading: Faculty Access
passages.text: Faculty members automatically have access to Kuali CM, as faculty are the users authorized to submit curricular proposals. If this is your first time accessing Kuali CM, sign in using your URI Microsoft 365 account.

passages.heading: Non-Faculty Access
passages.text:
Access to Kuali CM is also available to deans and select administrators or staff. In specific cases, other non-faculty users may request access.
Use the Kuali Access Package to request access using your URI SSO. After selecting Continue, you will be asked to provide your job or position title and a business justification for needing access. Once your request has been reviewed, you will be notified whether access has been granted.

passages.heading: Logging In
passages.text:
Sign in to your Microsoft 365 Apps using your URI SSO.
Select Kuali Course Management from your application collection.
Alternatively, use the direct link to Kuali CM and bookmark it for future access.

passages.heading: Accessing the Curriculum App
passages.text: Once logged in, select the Curriculum tile. This is where you can view current courses, programs, and specializations and, for authorized users, create proposals for new or modified curriculum.

passages.heading: The Kuali Dashboard
passages.text: When you enter Curriculum Management, the Dashboard serves as your homepage. It provides quick access to your proposals and items requiring your action.

passages.heading: My Proposals
passages.text:
My Proposals allows you to:
Continue working on Drafts you have started but not yet submitted.
View submitted proposals and their current workflow status.
Access proposals directly from the Dashboard.
Any proposals you begin but have not yet submitted will appear as Drafts. From this section, you can continue editing or delete a draft.
Select View All to see your complete list of proposals. The list can be filtered, downloaded, and printed.

passages.heading: My Action List
passages.text:
My Action List displays your ten most recent items requiring action. These may include proposals that require you to:
Review and approve
Acknowledge
Edit and return to the workflow after being sent back by a reviewing committee

passages.heading: Navigating Kuali
passages.text: Use the navigation bar on the left side of the screen to access courses, programs, specializations, and proposals, including drafts, proposals under review, and approved records.

passages.heading: 🔎 Search and Filters
passages.text:
Use the search bar at the top of the Courses, Programs, Specializations, or Proposals pages to locate specific records. Use the filters on the right side of the page to narrow your results.
Status: Select Active when searching for current curricular items. Retired and Inactive statuses are not consistently used in Kuali CM.
Groups: Use Groups to locate curricular records associated with a specific department or college.

passages.heading: Versioning
passages.text:
Kuali uses colored bars to indicate which version of a curricular record you are viewing.
🟢 Current Version — The version currently in effect. For most records, the earliest version available in Kuali is Fall 2022, when URI began using Kuali. Earlier historical versions are available in eCampus.
⚪ Past Version — An earlier version of the record, including inactive records.
🟣 Future Version — A version scheduled to become active in a future term.
↕️ Use the arrows next to the term dates to expand the record history and select an earlier or future version.

passages.heading: Proposal Status
passages.text:
The status indicators below apply only when you are viewing a proposal and not the curricular record itself. The colored bar at the top of a proposal indicates where the proposal is in the curriculum approval workflow.
🟡 Draft — A new proposal or proposed change that has been created but not yet submitted to the workflow. Drafts can be edited or deleted.
🔵 Under Review — A proposal that has been submitted to the workflow and is currently moving through the approval process.
⚫ Denied — A proposal that has been denied during the review process. Denied proposals cannot be edited or resubmitted.
🟢 Approved — A proposal that has completed the required approval process and has been approved.
Tip: When viewing an approved proposal, you can switch to the current curricular record by selecting “View Active Course (Program / Specialization).”

passages.heading: Course Description
passages.text:
Course Description
Tags: courses
Short Description: Student-facing summary of a course that clearly and concisely communicates its content, purpose, and focus.
Course Description
Course descriptions are written for students, not faculty, and must communicate clearly and concisely to them. Jargon, acronyms, and technical language should be avoided as much as possible. Anyone should be able to read the description and understand the nature and intent of the course.
An acceptable course description with a maximum of 30 words, begins with a verb, e.g. examines, introduces, explores, investigates. Articles, adjectives and adverbs are seldom necessary. Sentence fragments are acceptable.

passages.heading: The Approval Process
passages.text:
The curriculum approval process generally follows the sequence shown in the URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart. Specific steps may vary by college, department, proposal type, and whether the proposal requires additional levels of review.
URI Curricular Approval Process Flowchart

passages.heading: Overview
passages.text:
Proposal Development Faculty use the forms in Kuali Curriculum Management to develop the proposal and work with other stakeholders as appropriate.
Department Review The proposal is reviewed through the appropriate departmental process.
College Curriculum Committee Review The College Curriculum Committee reviews the proposal.
College Dean Approval The College Dean approves the proposal for Faculty Senate review.
Faculty Senate Curriculum Committee Review The Curriculum & Standards Committee, the General Education Committee, or the Graduate Council reviews the proposal.
Faculty Senate Approval The Faculty Senate considers the curriculum committee's recommendation and votes.
University President Approval Any curricular item that is not a course must be reviewed and approved by the University President.
URI Board of Trustees Approval In addition to the University President’s approval, new Majors and Degrees are also reviewed by the Board of Trustees.

Repeat Criteria
Tags: courses
Short Description: The criteria specifying how many times a course may be taken, the maximum credits that may be earned through repeated enrollment, and any restrictions on repeating the course within the same term.
Repeat Criteria
The criteria specifying the limits and conditions for repeating a course, including:
Maximum Enrollments: The maximum number of times a course may be taken.
Maximum Credits Allowed: The maximum number of credits that may be earned through repeated enrollment during a student’s academic career.
Same-Term Repeats: Whether the course may be repeated within the same term.
Maximum Credits Allowed Per Term: The maximum number of credits that may be taken through repeat enrollment in a single term.

Tags: programs
Short Description: The official title of a program as it appears in the academic catalog, including its required formatting.
Academic Program Title
Program titles entered in Kuali flow directly to the academic catalog and should follow the University’s established formatting conventions. Use the guidelines below to ensure program titles are presented consistently in the catalog.

passages.heading: Degree Programs: Formatting the Title for the Catalog
passages.text:
[Full Degree Name] - [Degree Abbreviation]
Examples:
Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies - BIS
Professional Science Masters - PSM
Doctor of Physical Therapy - DPT

passages.heading: Major Programs: Formatting the Title for the Catalog
passages.text:
[Major Title] - [Degree Abbreviation]
Examples:
French - BA
Dietetics - MS
Education - PhD

passages.heading: Minors: Formatting the Title for the Catalog
passages.text:
[Title of Minor] - Minor
Examples:
Family Finance - Minor
Textiles, Fashion Merchandising, and Design - Minor
Robotics Engineering - Minor

passages.heading: Certificate Programs: Formatting the Title for the Catalog
passages.text:
[Title of Certificate] - [Undergraduate or Graduate] [Online if applicable] Certificate
Examples:
Energy Economics and Policy - Undergraduate Certificate
Information Literacy Instruction - Graduate Certificate
Natural Resources and the Environment - Graduate Online Certificate

passages.heading: Content Overlap
passages.text:
Content Overlap
Tags: courses,programs,specializations
Short Description: Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial content overlap.
Content Overlap
Proposed courses, programs, and specializations are reviewed for potential content overlap with existing curricula. Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial actual or perceived content overlap.
Early consultation with potentially affected academic units may help identify concerns, clarify distinctions between offerings, and support an efficient review process.
A letter of support, which may be provided as an email from an affected department chair, can be uploaded to the Kuali proposal to document (a) that both departments have considered potential content overlap; (b) communication between the affected department and the department proposing the curriculum; and (c) the affected department’s support for the proposed curriculum.

passages.text:
Estimate the projected impact of the organizational change on the other public higher education institutions in Rhode Island (e.g., loss of students or revenues), provide a specific rationale of the assumptions make in the projections, and indicate the manner in which the other public institutions were consulted in developing the projections. Have you communicated with other institutions about the organizational change and have any concerns been raised related to role, scope, and mission or duplication?Response
List and describe any cooperative arrangements with other institutions relative to the organizational unit. (Signed copies of any agreements pertaining to the use of faculty, library, equipment, and facilities should be attached.)Response

FACILITIES AND CAPITAL EQUIPMENTFacilities and capital equipment should be sufficient in quantity, quality and timeliness to support the organizational change.
